answer.rationale: Timing is the strongest available signal: the release landed 2h ago and write-path p99 began climbing ~30 minutes later, so the release is the leading suspect. memory_b1 records a clean rollback that cleared a checkout error spike, and memory_b6 records that staged/canary gating surfaced regressions within an hour — together they support rolling back, and b6 specifically supports doing it in a gated cohort rather than fleet-wide. I want the archived source for both because b1 is a one-line consolidation of the exact maneuver I intend (I need to know whether that prior rollback was under heavy write load or during a quiet window, and whether 'no customer impact' was measured or assumed), and b6 tells me whether canary cohorts on this platform actually cover the write path or only the checkout read path. I am NOT verifying memory_b2: it already carries its own counterexample ('never fail over while writes are hot'), and settlement traffic is at daily peak with writes heavy, so regional_failover is ruled out by the very condition that caused the two lost accounts in March — that memory's caveat is the load-bearing part and it is intact. add_capacity (b3) was validated against a queue-depth surge, not a post-release latency regression, and provisioning takes longer than the degradation is trending; route_read_replicas (b5) fixed primary contention from report queries, which is a read-side cause that does not match a write-path climb starting after a deploy; enable_circuit_breaker (b4) contains a failing dependency but would shed settlement writes at peak, directly violating the do-not-lose-writes objective. Residual uncertainty I am deliberately holding open: the latency climb could be driven by settlement peak alone and merely coincident with the release, in which case rollback buys nothing and burns the single intervention window. That is exactly why I want the guarded cohort first — it distinguishes the two hypotheses at low blast radius before committing the fleet. Value risk flagged: rolling back with writes hot risks schema or message-format skew between the old build and records written by the new one, so the guarded rollback must confirm backward read/write compatibility before any ramp, and if the archive shows b1's rollback was performed on a cold write path I will treat its 'no customer impact' as not transferable to this situation.
